page_objective: Define how SIPANEL communicates project risks, technical challenges, engineering decisions, and preventive solutions with clarity, professionalism, and measurable credibility.

core_principle.statement: SIPANEL communicates risk as an engineering responsibility, not as fear-based marketing.
core_principle.communication_goal: Help project stakeholders understand technical risks clearly while demonstrating how engineering coordination reduces execution uncertainty.

principles.title: Explain Before Selling
principles.description: Clarify the engineering cause of a problem before presenting SIPANEL's solution.

principles.title: Use Technical Logic
principles.description: Support every risk statement with engineering reasoning or execution logic.

principles.title: Avoid Fear Marketing
principles.description: Communicate risk professionally without exaggeration or manipulation.

principles.title: Focus on Prevention
principles.description: Position SIPANEL as a system that prevents execution problems before they happen.

principles.title: Connect Risk to Measurable Impact
principles.description: Explain how technical mistakes affect leakage, waste, delays, rework, or hidden costs.

primary_risk_categories.description: Leakage caused by incorrect slope design, flashing details, overlap execution, or drainage coordination.
primary_risk_categories.preferred_message: Waterproofing performance depends on coordinated drainage, overlap detailing, and installation sequencing before execution begins.

primary_risk_categories.description: Excess panel usage caused by inaccurate layout planning or procurement mistakes.
primary_risk_categories.preferred_message: Accurate shop drawings and coordinated panel layouts help reduce unnecessary material waste and procurement errors.

primary_risk_categories.description: Site conflicts and installation interruptions caused by poor coordination.
primary_risk_categories.preferred_message: Pre-coordinated engineering documentation reduces installation interruptions and execution uncertainty.

primary_risk_categories.description: Incorrect alignment, fastening, or detailing that requires correction after installation.
primary_risk_categories.preferred_message: Controlled installation workflows reduce rework and improve execution accuracy.

primary_risk_categories.description: Unexpected costs caused by technical mistakes discovered late in execution.
primary_risk_categories.preferred_message: Engineering review before procurement helps identify hidden technical risks before they become expensive site problems.

recommended_structure: Support with proof or visual explanation

example.problem: Industrial roof leakage after heavy rain.
example.engineering_cause: Incorrect gutter slope and insufficient overlap detailing.
example.impact: Water infiltration, insulation damage, and maintenance cost.
example.sipanel_solution: Drainage logic and waterproofing details coordinated before installation.
example.proof: Shop drawing annotation and completed project reference.

forbidden_phrases: Your project will fail without us

proof_alignment_rules: Every risk claim should connect to technical reasoning.
Support major claims with case studies or diagrams.
Do not publish unverified performance numbers.
Risk communication must increase trust, not anxiety.

risk_to_solution_mapping.solution: Drainage slope planning and waterproofing detail coordination
Optimized shop drawing and BOM / MTO control

requirements: Maintain technical accuracy in all translations.
Avoid exaggerated wording in any language.
Support RTL layouts for Persian and Arabic.

implementation_notes: Risk communication should position SIPANEL as a technically responsible engineering partner.
Avoid using fear to drive conversion.
Technical clarity and preventive logic must always be more important than emotional persuasion.
All risk communication should reinforce trust, engineering discipline, and execution control.
